bootstrapAuthority.name: evaluator
bootstrapAuthority.note: Frozen spike.md bootstrap process exception: Spike 012 evaluator prepare and verify both execute under this pinned pre-implementation evaluator skill; the newly implemented repair mode and correction-cycle authority are implementation under test.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC01; "Core model", scope 1; DM "Shared contracts"
criteria.sufficiency: AC01 is the distinct-cycle-identity claim; E1 shows one cycle spanning multiple implementation and verification attempts with the evaluator-revision and executor/process-attempt identities never folded into the cycle identity, and S6 confirms the authority code represents cycle identity as its own append-only identifier space separate from the other four.

AC02 requires legacy history to read as Cycle 001 without rewriting it; E2 runs an unannotated pre-cycle history through the updated authority and shows it interpreted as Cycle 001 with the historical bytes untouched, and S6 confirms the authority derives that from the append-only history rather than retrofitting cycle fields into legacy events.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC03; "Human rejection closes a cycle", scope 1, 3; DM "Design decisions"
criteria.sufficiency: AC03 is the IMPLEMENTATION_GAP-opens-exactly-one-same-spike-cycle claim; E3 opens a correction cycle from such a rejection, asserts the opening binds the unchanged frozen brief and Design Map identities, and shows a second opening from the same rejection refused.
AC04 requires an EVALUATOR_COVERAGE_DEFECT rejection to open a cycle that requires evaluator repair; E4 opens such a cycle and asserts the opening evidence records evaluator repair as required.

AC05 is the both-findings claim; E5 opens a correction cycle from a rejection carrying an implementation finding and an evaluator finding and asserts the opening records both implementation correction and evaluator repair as required.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC06; "Spike 011 recovery proof", scope 2; DM "Invariants"
criteria.sufficiency: AC06 requires a deterministic fixture to recognize Spike 011's primary+secondary rejection as Cycle-002-eligible without editing Spike 011; E6 is that fixture, asserting Cycle-001 interpretation, both-correction eligibility, and preserved Cycle 001 brief/Design Map identities, and P2 confirms spikes/011-host-owned-workflow-runs/** is byte-for-byte unchanged.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC07; "Human rejection closes a cycle", scope 15; DM "Design decisions"
criteria.sufficiency: AC07 is the SPECIFICATION_CHANGE-cannot-open, successor-lineage-still-required claim; E7 shows such a rejection refused for correction-cycle opening while the successor path stays available, and S5 confirms the authority code still routes specification-changing rejections to the successor / new-brief lineage.
AC08 is the no-reopen-after-acceptance claim; E8 human-accepts a cycle and shows every correction-cycle opening from it refused.

AC09 requires Cycle 001 completion facts not to satisfy Cycle 002 prerequisites; E9 gives Cycle 001 PASS/promotion/As-Built/decision and shows Cycle 002 still reporting each of its own prerequisites unmet until it meets them, with Cycle 001 state unchanged.

AC10 is the implementation-attempt-legal-after-human-IMPLEMENTATION_GAP-without-a-fabricated-failed-verification claim; E10 opens a correction cycle with an implementation-correction finding and shows a new implementation attempt accepted with no preceding failed evaluator verification in that cycle.
AC11 preserves the existing in-cycle retry path; E11 shows a failed technical verification still permitting a further implementation attempt and re-verification within the same cycle.

AC12 is a property of the evaluator skill file at the implementation commit; S1 reads the skill and confirms three explicit modes prepare/verify/repair with documented non-overlapping responsibilities and an integer contract version greater than 10.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC13; scope 7, 12, "Verify discovers defects"; DM "Invariants"
criteria.sufficiency: AC13 requires verify not to mutate the frozen evaluator and to finalize/record a discovered defect before repair; E12 shows a verify attempt staying bound to its revision, finalized forward-only on a discovered defect, with no corrected revision usable until a separate repair, and S2 confirms the verify mode text forbids in-attempt mutation and mandates finalize-then-record.

AC14 requires an authoritative defect trigger and rejection of an ungrounded repair; E13 shows repair proceeding from a finalized EVALUATOR_DEFECT attempt or a closed EVALUATOR_COVERAGE_DEFECT cycle and refused when given only a free-text reason, and S2 confirms the repair mode text and code require that binding.

AC15 requires a successful repair to preserve the source revision and create a distinguishable new one; E14 asserts the source revision is byte-for-byte intact after repair and the new revision carries a distinct identifier and content identity.

AC16 requires the repair to be bounded to the demonstrated defect and not to rerun full prepare as a required step; E14 diffs the two revisions and shows only defect-related artifacts changed (unrelated ones identical in content identity), and S2 confirms the repair mode text scopes the semantic change to the defect and does not mandate a full semantic re-derivation.

AC17 requires the whole resulting revision to pass structural integrity validation before becoming current; E15 shows repair running the complete deterministic validation over the entire resulting revision and a failing result blocking the revision from becoming current, and S2 confirms the repair mode text requires that whole-revision re-validation.

AC18 forbids repair changing the frozen brief, Design Map, public eval-requirements.md, or acceptance semantics; E16 shows each such repair attempt refused while an evidence-only swap that establishes the same frozen criterion is allowed, and S2 confirms the repair mode text forbids those changes.

AC19 requires repair to block, not silently change public authority, when a materially new public seam or product requirement is needed; E16 shows that block-and-classify path, S2 confirms the repair mode text mandates it, and S5 confirms the authority routes such cases onto the successor / methodology path.

AC20 enumerates the immutable repair-record contents; E17 asserts every completed or terminally blocked repair produces a record and public-safe binding carrying the repair id, trigger type/identity, source/result revision identifiers and identities, affected criteria/procedures, defect and correction descriptions, changed-artifact identities, the semantic-preservation attestation, the frozen authority identities, and the integrity result.

AC21 is the durable attempt-to-revision binding plus monotonic non-reused identifiers; E14 shows every verification attempt still resolving to the exact revision it executed after a repair, with revision and attempt identifiers monotonic and never reused.

AC22 requires authority and promotion evidence to distinguish revisions and repair lineage without overwriting earlier evidence; E18 names and distinguishes revision 001, revision 002, and the repair lineage between them and shows promoting the later revision leaving the earlier frozen/promoted evidence intact.

AC23 requires multi-finding human rejection plus legacy compatibility; E19 records a primary classification plus additional typed findings and reads Spike 011's classification+secondaryFinding record through the same normalized finding set without rewriting that event.

AC24 requires a new cycle to run its own full sequence; E20 shows the opened cycle recording its own implementation handoff, verification allocation and PASS, promotion, As-Built, and a fresh human decision, each checked against that cycle's own prerequisites.

AC25 enumerates the status-surface fields; E21 asserts the public authority status surface exposes the current cycle identity and open/closed state, current evaluator revision, current implementation attempt, current/final verification state, cycle-scoped promotion/As-Built/human state, correction permission and reason, and lineage, with historical cycles still distinguishable and no manual JSONL parsing required.

AC26 forbids an unnecessary human gate before the next decision; E22 shows a mechanically-authorized correction-cycle opening and an evaluator-defect-to-repair flow each proceeding without a new human approval gate, while the next acceptance/rejection remains a human decision.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC27; "Evaluator skill versioning and bootstrap", "Verification of the bootstrap boundary"; DM "Shared contracts"
criteria.sufficiency: AC27 requires both evaluator phases to run under an exact provenance-verifiable pre-implementation skill identity with a mechanism proving no substitution; S3 confirms bootstrap/evaluator-skill.md equals the pinned skill, bootstrap/evaluator-authority.json binds its provenance, and the dispatcher supplies that pinned material for the Spike 012 evaluator phases, and P3 confirms the freeze and the verification result both cite the bootstrap-authority identity and no post-implementation skill identity.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC28; "Bootstrap evaluator defects", "Bootstrap human rejection", "Verification of the bootstrap boundary"; DM "Invariants"
criteria.sufficiency: AC28 forbids Spike 012 using its own new repair/correction-cycle facilities to grade or recover itself before acceptance; S4 confirms Spike 012's workflow.jsonl and evaluation/** carry no correction-cycle-opened or evaluator-repair-recorded transition and the cycle is governed by the pinned v10 contract, and P3 confirms no Spike 012 evaluator evidence cites the new facilities.

AC29 requires visible deterministic regression coverage of the four behaviour families without live paid-provider calls; E23 asserts that coverage exists in test/ for the correction-cycle, evaluator-repair, legacy-history, and successor-boundary behaviours, and P1 confirms the visible suite runs green through npm test with no live provider call.

AC30 is a set of command exit codes plus continued green pre-existing suites at the evaluated commit; P1 records npm test, typecheck, lint, format:check, git diff --check, and the workflow-authority, evaluator-integrity, host-owned workflow-run, and session/backend suites.
